newsitem.title: GREECE: Athens bourse falls sharply at opening.
newsitem.headline: Athens bourse falls sharply at opening.

text.p: The Athens bourse fell sharply at the open on Thursday, sinking through the 900-point barrier, as trading began to return to normal levels after a four-day interruption caused by a settlement scandal.

The bourse was down 1.34 pct, or 12.21 points, at 896.21 after 30 minutes. Under a deal between the brokers association and the national economy ministry brokerages had until 0900 this morning to settle their accounts at the clearing house to begin trading again.
Brokers attributed the sell-off to the upheavals which have rocked the bourse for the past week, and effectively stopped all trading for four days.
"You weren't expecting a rally today, were you?," asked one broker.
The crisis was triggered last week when Delta Securities tried to settle its account at the bourse clearing house with bad cheques.

The 65-member Association of Athens Stock Exchange Members (SMEXA), angered by perceived inaction by authorities to probe the Delta scandal, refused to trade last Friday and effectively closed the bourse for four days.
When the exchange opened on Thursday for the first normal session in a week, bourse authorities quickly ordered a two-day suspension of trade in four stocks linked to the Delta settlement scandal.
Magrizos, Parnassos, Hellenic Sugar Industry and St George Mills were suspended from trading on Thursday and Friday, a bourse statement said.
"The suspension is not related to the companies or their economic situations but is to facilitate any possible checks being conducted on transactions in their shares to date," it said.
